heading: INT. FUNERAL PARLOUR - SIDE ROOM - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. FUNERAL PARLOUR - SIDE ROOM - AFTERNOON
A narrow room of dusty velvet.
A tea urn steams in the corner.
The funeral next door has just ended; muffled organ music drifts through the wall.
On a cloth-draped table, a photograph of an elderly man in a fishing hat.
Five mourners remain.
MAEVE FINNEGAN (70s, widow, black dress, chin high) stands at the photograph, straightening it for the third time.
Her sons: DECLAN (40s, suit too tight, tie pulled loose) leans on the urn and drinks from a styrofoam cup, and BRENDAN (40s, rumpled, red-eyed) sits on a folding chair staring at his shoes.
Their cousin AOIFE (30s, bright scarf) pours milk into her tea with great concentration.
And a stranger, a man in a rain-darkened trench coat, lingers by the door: MR. THADDEUS KRANE (60s, thin, polite).
Nobody speaks.
Ma. Sit down.
units.name: DECLAN

units.text: I'm fine standing.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: You've been on your feet since seven.
units.name: DECLAN

units.text: So has he.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: She nods at the photograph.
Declan lowers the cup.
Brendan lets out a small, wet laugh and wipes his nose with his wrist.
Would anyone like a biscuit?
units.name: AOIFE

units.text: I would.
units.name: BRENDAN

units.text: They're stale.
units.name: DECLAN

units.text: I don't care.
units.name: BRENDAN

units.text: She brings him the plate.
He takes one, holds it, doesn't eat.
Maeve turns from the photograph and looks at the stranger by the door.
You're not family.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: No, madam.
units.name: KRANE

units.text: Then who are you?
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: I worked with your husband. Years ago. At the shipyard.
units.name: KRANE

units.text: Frank never said.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: He wouldn't have. We weren't friends.
units.name: KRANE

units.text: Then why are you here?
units.name: DECLAN

units.text: Because he did me a kindness once. And I never repaid it.
units.name: KRANE

units.text: Maeve crosses the room, slowly, shoes clicking.
She stops in front of him, studies his face, and takes his hands in both of hers.
Take your coat off. You'll catch your death.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: Madam, I really should go.
units.name: KRANE

units.text: You'll have tea.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: It isn't a question.
Krane lets her pull the coat off his shoulders.
She hands it to Aoife, who hangs it carefully.
Declan and Brendan exchange a glance.
Then Brendan, abruptly, pushes the plate of biscuits across the table toward the stranger.
They're stale.
units.name: BRENDAN

units.text: So I understand.
units.name: KRANE

units.text: He takes one.
Maeve pours a cup, hands it to him, and for a moment the only sound is the muffled organ from next door, carrying one slow chord after another, and the clink of five spoons in five cups.
Then the music stops.
A door opens somewhere in the building.
Footsteps, voices, laughter.
The funeral is over.
They stand in the quiet and do not go out.
